about: Real yeast RNA-seq read pairs, chosen for adapters, for adapter and quality trimming (cutadapt, fastp). Taken unchanged from the test data of the genomics-wasm project (github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, commit bfacba302b32f9fe12da4cc694c9a0b65b492986: datasets/cutadapt/yeast, whose manifest.json records every source and step, and README.md the selection).
run: SRR6357070 (wild-type total RNA-seq, biological replicate 1; GEO GSE110004; Illumina HiSeq 2500; 101-base paired reads)
publication: Wu et al. (2018) Molecular Cell, doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2018.10.018
source: nf-core/test-datasets, commit cad884e7fbe5617dcd55bdd07d9ddf65b54febe4: testdata/GSE110004/SRR6357070_1.fastq.gz and _2.fastq.gz (50,000 pairs that nf-core selected for chromosome I)
selection: The first 96 pairs, in source order, of each of four groups, taken in this order: (1) both reads contain their whole 33-base adapter; (2) either read contains AGATCGGAAGAGC; (3) either read has a base quality below 20 in its last 10 bases; (4) all other pairs. The FASTQ records are copied unchanged, in their original order. The selection makes adapters far more common than in the run itself.

adapters.note: sequences that occur in these reads; no particular kit is implied

nativeCutadapt52: cutadapt -a <read1 adapter> -A <read2 adapter>: 205 first and 209 second reads with the adapter; 12,061 bases removed
licence: MIT (nf-core/test-datasets); the reads are public INSDC data
